name: Tempester n°26: the project request (n°24) sends without drawing on the screen
explanation: n°24 serves the request F0 01 28 42 F7 by calling the menu's sender [routine], which draws its progress lines (« Exporting Project Params... Done », « Exporting Project Beat n ») into the frame buffer and pushes the whole buffer to the LCD ([routine] -> [routine]), so over whatever screen is shown, where they stay unreadable (seen on the machine by the author, 2026-11-08). Of the 43 functions reachable from the sender, only the sender itself calls a screen routine, and all its screen calls ([routine] x5, [routine], [routine] x2, text width [routine] x4, number to text [routine] x2) and its drawing-colour stores sit in three self-contained blocks ([address]-[address], [address]-[address], [address]-[address]) that send nothing; their x / y locals are used nowhere else. Fix: one word per block jumps to a gate in free flash (0x9d07cb00-0x9d07cb5f): while a request 42 is served (SysEx command [address] = 0x42, written only by [routine] and reset by n°24's [routine](0) after the send) the gate jumps over the block; otherwise, i.e. the menu « Export Project over MIDI », it executes the replaced instruction and resumes the block, so the menu's screen is unchanged. Result: a request sends the same bytes as before (and as the menu) and touches neither the frame buffer, the LCD nor the drawing colour; the screen shown before the request stays as it was. Requires n°24 (the request) and n°2d (the sender's frame, whose words are not touched). No RAM added. Docs/analyses/feature-project-request.md §9.
